items.t: Sony Group stock: RSU share disposal caps a week of filings
sum: Sony Group's investor-relations calendar showed two filings during the week of November 9 through November 13. The announcements add a corporate-action item and a reporting milestone to the outlook for investors.

On Friday, November 13, Sony announced the planned disposal of treasury shares after restricted stock units vest. The filing, carried by StockTitan, sets the payment date for 6,273,892 shares at December 1, 2026, at a disposal price of 4,281 yen per share. A further 26,878 shares are scheduled for cash settlement during the period from December 1 through December 15.

The filing says the shares relate to Sony's compensation plan for vested RSUs. The number of shares may be reduced before settlement under the plan rules, so the announced amount is a scheduled figure rather than a completed transfer.

On Tuesday, November 10, Sony's Investor Relations page listed the semi-annual securities report for the six months ended September 30, 2026. The filing gives investors a formal reporting reference alongside the company's second-quarter materials released earlier in November.
Sony Group stock traded at 24.45 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:12 CET on Saturday, November 14.

sum: Japan’s Nikkei index closed lower on Thursday, erasing earlier gains as technology stocks came under pressure from deepening losses in Nasdaq futures, while shares of Nvidia plummeted in after-hours trading.
According to Reuters, Nvidia shares fell by more than 8% in after-hours trading following a report by The Wall Street Journal that the company is preparing to dismiss its CEO, Jensen Huang.

A source familiar with the matter told Reuters that Nvidia’s board of directors is set to hold a meeting to decide on Huang’s removal. The company—the world’s largest supplier of artificial intelligence chips—is currently grappling with the fallout from reports concerning two extramarital affairs involving its CEO.
The Nikkei index fell 0.7% to 60,819.84 points, having risen by 0.88% earlier in the session. Meanwhile, the broader Topix index rose 0.2% to 3,937.33 points.

Takamasa Ikeda, a senior portfolio manager at GCI Asset Management, stated, "Traders anticipated a decline on Wall Street later today, given the drop in Nasdaq futures during Asian trading." "Investors also took into account the sell-off in Nvidia shares during after-hours trading," he added.
In Tokyo, shares of Advantest—a supplier with ties to Nvidia—fell 4.64%, while shares of Ibiden plunged 8.32%.
Ibiden recorded the largest percentage loss among the stocks on the Nikkei index.

sum: Nvidia is facing one of its sharpest selloffs in recent months, with shares falling 5.5% on Tuesday to close at $168.47. The decline extends the stock's losses to roughly 10% since Friday and nearly 18% this month, as investors react to growing scrutiny surrounding CEO Jensen Huang, renewed interest rate concerns, and uncertainty ahead of the company's upcoming earnings report.

The latest Nvidia price prediction now hinges on whether the chipmaker can regain investor confidence while maintaining its strong AI-driven earnings growth. Despite the recent weakness, Wall Street analysts remain broadly optimistic about Nvidia's long-term prospects, while CoinCodex forecasts suggest a gradual recovery through the end of 2026 and stronger gains in 2027.
Nvidia shares slide as Jensen Huang investigation raises concerns

Nvidia's latest decline follows reports that CEO Jensen Huang is facing scrutiny over an alleged relationship with a woman suspected of having connections to Chinese intelligence. The controversy has raised questions about potential national security implications and whether Nvidia's business dealings in China could face additional regulatory attention.

According to recent reporting, the relationship may have been connected to the shipment of billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips through Chinese companies. President Donald Trump confirmed that the FBI was looking into the matter, although he also expressed confidence that Huang would ultimately be in good shape.

Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation into the allegations, with outside legal counsel supporting the review. The company has emphasized that it currently has no reason to believe confidential information or US national security has been compromised, while maintaining confidence in Huang's leadership.

The uncertainty has nevertheless weighed heavily on Nvidia shares. The stock initially fell sharply on Monday, briefly erasing approximately $350 billion in market capitalization, before extending its decline on Tuesday.

A soft quarter is taking a back seat to blockbuster preorder demand at one of gaming’s biggest publishers. Take-Two Interactive (NASDAQ:TTWO | TTWO Price Prediction) stock is at $223.49 in morning trading, up 8%. The company reported its fiscal Q2 2027 results late on November 9, and management’s comments on Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) preorders are doing the heavy lifting.

CEO Strauss Zelnick spoke on the earnings call. He said, “Pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are tracking far in excess of our initial expectations and we know that the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough.” Chief Financial Officer Lainie Goldstein called the level of preorders “extraordinary.” Take-Two’s gain comes as shareholders position for the launch.

Take-Two’s GTA VI arrives November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with a standard edition at $79.99 and an Ultimate Edition at $99.99. Strauss Zelnick cited the extended game preview. It premiered on Netflix (NASDAQ:NFLX) and drew 31 million consumers in its first four days, becoming the platform’s most viewed title for the week.

Quarterly revenue at Take-Two fell 15.6% year over year to $1.50 billion, missing the $1.66 billion consensus estimate. Net bookings at the company dropped 18% to $1.60 billion, and Lainie Goldstein noted that the result came in below the company’s guidance range of $1.62 billion to $1.67 billion. Management also disclosed that NBA 2K27 fell short of its forecast for the period.

On a GAAP basis, Take-Two lost $0.29 per share, a much narrower loss than the $0.86 analysts expected. A $57.9 million income tax benefit helped that comparison, and before taxes and other items the company posted an operating loss of $117.5 million.

Take-Two reiterated its fiscal 2027 net bookings outlook of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion and raised its fiscal 2027 GAAP revenue forecast to $7.98 billion to $8.18 billion. For fiscal Q3 2027, the company expects net bookings of $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion. Zelnick explained why the preorder strength isn’t in the numbers yet, saying, “We tend to avoid claiming success before it occurs.”

Alanis Morissette Shares She Identifies as Pansexual
sum: Alanis Morissette identifies as pansexual, she revealed in a podcast appearance earlier this week. The hitmaker — who just dropped her first holiday album, Good Weather for Immaculate Conception, featuring new single “To an Empath at Christmas Time” — visited the Handsome Podcast as the podcast trio’s first in-person guest for an episode that was uploaded on Nov. 3.

“I’m sorry for the men that hurt you, but I’m not sorry for the songs that came from it. Those are pretty amazing,” comedian Fortune Feimster, who co-hosts the show with Tig Notaro and Mae Martin, said at one point toward the end of the episode, adding, “Did it make you want to be a lesbian at any point?”
“I’m pansexual, so yeah,” Morissette shared in reply. “I get everything.”
Notaro then asked, “Wait, you’re not really pansexual, are you?” to which Morissette confirmed, “I am.”
Joking that they should’ve launched the episode with this tidbit, Notaro said, “How did I not know this?”
“You know, I like to leave it for the epilogue,” quipped Morissette. “I like to confuse people on the way out. Is it confusing?”

Morissette, who’s got three Billboard 200 No. 1 albums under her belt and whose top hit “Ironic” soared to No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1996, is married to husband Mario Treadway, aka the artist Souleye. The couple wed in 2010 and are parents to three children.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Begins Rebound as U.S. Stock Gains and Oil Price Plunge Offer Support, but AI and Semiconductor Shares Weigh
sum: The Nikkei 225 began trading higher on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on November 5, opening at 62,384.73 yen, up 196.10 yen (0.32%) from the previous trading day. Buying led the market, carrying over the momentum from gains in all three major U.S. stock indexes the prior day.

Two factors pushed the market up. One was the firm performance of the U.S. stock market as it digested the results of the U.S. midterm elections. The other was a sharp drop in crude oil prices as views spread that tensions in the Middle East were easing. Lower energy costs support investor sentiment through both corporate earnings and household burdens.
Among blue-chip shares, Toyota Motor (7203.T) surged, while Sony Group (6758.T) and index-heavyweight Fast Retailing (9983.T) were quoted higher.

On the other hand, artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor-related shares saw notable declines. SoftBank Group (9984.T), Tokyo Electron (8035.T), and Advantest (6857.T) all fell sharply, as caution over the direction of AI regulation continued to simmer.

In the previous day's trading on November 4, these three semiconductor and AI-related stocks alone pushed the Nikkei 225 down by about 1,241 yen at one point. Selling tends to concentrate in stocks with large index weightings, and this structure continues to amplify swings across the broader market.

Among market participants, the near-term focus is whether buybacks will emerge in the sharply fallen semiconductor shares. On the previous day, some stocks such as Fast Retailing and Nintendo (7974.T) rose, so the market was not uniformly lower. Some see the fact that buying interest is not one-sided as a sign of the market's underlying resilience.

On the overseas front, reports on vote counting in the U.S. midterm elections were also coming in during Tokyo trading hours, and market participants are focused on how U.S. long-term interest rates and foreign exchange rates react. Domestically, earnings announcements from companies such as IHI (7013.T), Mitsubishi Corp (8058.T), and NTT (9432.T) are scheduled during trading hours, and stock price reactions to individual earnings results could divide winners and losers within sectors.

items.t: Sony Group Corp Stock (SONY) Moved Down by 4.07% on Sep 8: What Signal Does It Send?
sum: Sony Group Corp (SONY) moved down by 4.07%. The Technology Equipment sector is up by 0.75%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: NVIDIA Corp (NVDA) down 1.94%; Micron Technology Inc (MU) up 0.29%; Intel Corp (INTC) up 9.55%.

Sony Group Corporation experienced downside pressure and elevated intraday volatility during the trading session, reflecting broad sector rotation and macroeconomic headwinds across equity markets. Following the holiday weekend, major indices came under strain as escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East drove crude oil prices higher, stoking concerns over persistent inflationary pressure. Coupled with tight labor market metrics, market expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike at the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting remained elevated. High-beta technology, consumer hardware, and international growth-oriented equities bore the brunt of this shift, as rising Treasury yields and tighter monetary prospects compressed valuation multiples across consumer electronics and media conglomerates.

Beyond macro-level factors, investor sentiment was influenced by segment-specific friction within Sony's Gaming and Network Services division. Market participants evaluated public pushback and operational adjustments surrounding the company's long-term digital strategy, particularly discussions regarding the eventual phaseout of physical game discs on the PlayStation platform. Ongoing consumer debate and legal considerations highlighted potential execution risks in platform transition timelines. Additionally, industry-wide concerns regarding component cost inflation, supply chain logistics, and trade policy tariffs continued to foster investor caution around hardware margin expansion, tempering immediate enthusiasm ahead of the upcoming key software release cycle.

From an institutional research perspective, the session's weakness reflects short-term market rebalancing and risk reduction rather than a breakdown in the company's core fundamental thesis. Sony's diversified entertainment flywheel—anchored by high-margin music publishing, theatrical distribution, and proprietary intellectual property—provides a strong operational cushion against cyclical downturns.

A Sony Interactive Entertainment spokesperson told Gamespot: "Players can continue to access and play their purchased games as usual. A one-time online check is required to confirm the game's license, after which no further check-ins are required."

When purchasing a game on the PS Store, players buy a digital license to download, install and play a game. Instead of having a physical disc, this game is tied to the player's account and can be downloaded any time on consoles.

There had been widespread claims that with new purchases from March 2026, players have to connect their account to the internet every 30 days or else they will lose access to games they have purchased digitally - even if they have paid full price for the license of a game, downloaded it and want to continue playing offline.
Before Sony shared that statement, a number of players took it upon themselves to find out what exactly was going on and found Sony may actually just be stopping license exploits with temporary DRMs.

According to a number of different players who tested it out, it appears Sony has introduced a temporary 14-day DRM with it turning into a permanent one after that once an active internet connection has been established or the user logs in to their account.

That means after a 14-day refund period, digital PlayStation games switch to a permanent license when the user signs in. PlayStation's terms of sale say digital games and DLC can be refunded within 14 days of purchase as long as the content has not started downloading or streaming.

How Taylor Swift’s Record Contract Could Lead to Millions of Dollars for UMG Artists After Spotify Stock Sale
sum: Universal Music Group chairman and CEO Lucian Grainge said on Tuesday (April 29) in an earnings call that the company’s board had approved the sale of half of UMG’s equity stake in Spotify, and that a portion of the proceeds will go to UMG artists.

But none of that was accidental, as UMG artist Taylor Swift sings in “Mastermind.” In March 2018, UMG pledged to give artists a share in any future Spotify divestment, following similar commitments from Warner Music Group and Sony Music Group. Seven months later, when Swift announced she was leaving her longtime label home, Big Machine, to join UMG’s Republic Records in November 2018, she said she negotiated a clause in her contract specifying that any such payout could not be clawed back.

In announcing the deal on Instagram, the “Shake It Off” singer wrote, “As part of my new contract with Universal Music Group, I asked that any sale of their Spotify shares result in a distribution of money to their artists, non-recoupable. They have generously agreed to this, at what they believe will be much better terms than paid out previously than other major labels.”

At the time, that distinction — recoupable or non-recoupable — was at the heart of an industry conversation around labels sharing divestiture revenue with artists. When Warner and Sony first announced in 2016 that they would share any profits from a sale of a stake in the streaming service with artists, there were concerns that any money earmarked for creators would be applied to outstanding advances, and that many artists would not actually receive these proceeds. Warner and Sony later clarified that they would structure payouts to artists according to their record contract terms; Sony said specifically it would not factor in recoupable balances. Two years later, when UMG said it would also share this income with artists, the company did not specify whether it would factor in recoupment — until Swift’s deal was announced in November.
That could be a big boon for many artists, including those who still owe back advances to the labels that initially signed them.

Nintendo shares slide on fears of rising Mideast shipping costs
sum: Nintendo’s shares fell the most in almost a month, hurt by fears that rerouted shipments in the wake of U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran may drive up logistics costs for Europe-bound Switch 2 consoles.

The world’s largest container carriers are rerouting services away from the Suez Canal and sending vessels around the southern tip of Africa, after Houthi militants threatened to restart attacks on cargo ships in the Red Sea with ties to the U.S. and Israel. The move is estimated to add more than 10 days to deliveries.

Nintendo relies heavily on sea freight to transport its $450 console from assembly hubs in Asia. Its shares fell as much as 4.7% in Tokyo on Monday, underperforming the benchmark TOPIX’s decline. Shares of Sony, which also ships its PlayStation 5 consoles by sea, fell as much as 3%.

“As investors assess the broader impact of the Iran situation on the technology sector, game consoles will draw scrutiny because managing shipping costs are critical, given the thin profit margins on hardware,” said Toyo Securities analyst Hideki Yasuda.

The prospect of higher freight costs adds to the challenges facing the Kyoto-based company, which is already contending with tariffs on U.S.-bound Switch 2 units and losses on a Japan-only budget model sold at below cost. The Middle East has been an expanding market for game consoles, and prolonged disruption could slow that growth while weighing on near-term sales for hardware makers.

Plans by Nintendo’s shareholders to sell as much as ¥285.7 billion ($1.9 billion) worth of stakes in the company also weighed on the stock. Nintendo plans to repurchase as much as ¥100 billion of stock to cushion the impact.

Affiliate Pokemon on Friday said Pokemon Winds and Pokemon Waves — the next mainline installments in its blockbuster franchise — will be released in 2027, which was later than anticipated. Pokemon titles have historically helped drive Nintendo platform momentum, and a holiday-season release had been expected to boost otherwise lackluster software sales for the Switch 2.

This mysterious Sony camera was spotted at the 2026 Winter Olympics. But what is it?
sum: The Olympic Games bring some of the most talented athletes to an international stage – and some highly talented sports photographers along with them. The Olympics, then, naturally sometimes serve as proving grounds for up-and-coming sports cameras – which makes this disguised Sony camera spotted on the sidelines all the more intriguing.

Getty and photographer Eyes Wide Open shared a photo of two Sony cameras resting on a ledge in what looks like the press box during a preliminary round of Women’s Ice Hockey between Germany and Japan on February 07, in Milan, Italy.

The caption identifies the camera as “A Sony photo camera in prototype design.” A Sony logo is clearly seen on the camera’s battery grip, and there’s the orange 'G' logo associated with Sony’s G Master optics visible on the lens as well.

The cameras are wearing a skin commonly known as dazzle camouflage – it’s a black-and-white intricate pattern that’s designed to hide features and body lines. It’s commonly used to hide prototype cars, but could also be used to disguise cameras.

While the black-and-white pattern is often used for hiding a prototype design, it’s worth noting that custom camera skins like this exist and are easy to purchase – so it’s entirely possible that the camera is just a Sony A9 III wearing a fancy outfit, much in the same way that Olympic fans dress up for the event.
Another camera sits behind it in an opposite design – it could be a photographer's strategy for quickly identifying two of the same model cameras.

But, at the same time, it wouldn’t be too unusual to test a new prototype at such a high-caliber event. The Canon EOS R3, for example, was used at the 2020 Olympics in Tokyo prior to the camera’s full release, as was the Nikon Z9.

As for securing a supply of memory, we are already in a position to secure the minimum quantity necessary to manage the year-end selling season of next fiscal year. Going forward, we intend to further negotiate with various suppliers to secure enough supply to meet the demand of our customers.

items.t: Cheaper region-locked PS5 targets Switch 2, with Sony taking losses to regain support in Japan
sum: Sony's announcement of a region-locked PS5 at a recent State of Play surprised some fans. While other buyers face PS5 price increases, the Japan-exclusive console will cost ¥55,000 ($355). A new TV Tokyo report reveals that the move is a direct response to the localized Switch 2. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) CEO Hideaki Nishino aims to turn around the declining PS5 sales in the country.

Key points from the Japanese video were translated by Hartmann, an Install Base forum member. The broadcast confirms that Sony decided to release a cheaper console to mirror Nintendo’s strategy. According to the report, executives signed off on the PS5 price cut four months after the June Switch 2 release date.

At ¥49,980 ($322), the Switch 2 connects only to the Japanese eShop and has language restrictions. While these measures thwart international scalpers, it’s unclear if Nintendo profits from the hardware. In Sony’s case, TV Tokyo explains that the company is willing to sacrifice profits resulting from a lower PS5 price.

With a price cut of around $120, the decision may seem like a gamble for PlayStation. Even so, Hideaki Nishino wants to reverse a trend that accelerated in the PS3 era. Sony made a conscious decision to prioritize the global market at the expense of smaller Japanese developers. These studios also found it difficult to produce much more costly HD games.

Nishino didn’t assume his post until April 1st, 2025. In a departure from past leadership, he is again focusing on the domestic market. However, it may be difficult for PlayStation to match Nintendo’s furious pace.

By November 2025, as Push Square highlights, the Switch 2 had already sold 2.6 million units in Japan. By comparison, PS5 sales only total around 7 million, even with some versions debuting in 2020. The more affordable region-locked PS5 may address the particularly slow sales of the digital console.
Sony could capitalize on the lucrative mobile user base in Japan with the rumored PS6 handheld. For now, Nishino hopes to set the stage for a revival in PlayStation’s homeland.

sum: Sony had its Q2 earnings call today, November 11, where it shared an update on its businesses. While talking about the gaming segment, specifically hardware, one of the executives spoke about the PS5 and its continued support, for many years to come. That’s great news for those who just bought a PS5 ($499 on Amazon) or were planning to do so in the near future.

During the Q and A round of the call, when asked about the future strategy for the PS5, Sony Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Lin Tao spoke about how there are still a large number of users on the PS4, even though that console was launched over a decade ago. Because of this, Sony believes that the PS5 is only in the middle of its journey. The full quote is as follows:

Our view is that compared to conventional console life cycles, looking at the PS4 life cycle, it seems to be getting longer and longer. Especially the PS4 which was launched in 2013 and it’s been over a decade since then, but there are many active users enjoying the console. So, from that perspective, we believe that the PS5 is only in the middle of the journey and we are really planning to expand it even further.

This essentially means that support and development for the PS5 will continue for years to come, even after the PS6 launches in 2027 or 2028. It is unlikely that Sony is hinting at a delayed launch for the PS6 as the PS4 is still supported, though now with developers starting to step away from the console, alongside the PS5. By the time the PS6 releases, there will be even more users on the PS5 so it makes sense to continue development for that large user base, both from Sony and the game developer’s perspective.
